title: Book Two · Chapter 63: The Long Throw
story:
On Monday, Leo comes to school with a sore shoulder. He can carry his bag, but he does not want to throw the ball.

“Did the reading room do that?” Ronan asks.

Leo shakes his head. “A long game with my cousin.”

“Did you win?”

“I threw farther. Now he can move his arm.”

Jun lifts the ball. “We can roll it.”

Ronan looks at the ground. He thinks only very small children roll a ball. He wants to throw against the high mark on the wall.

Leo starts to sit on the step. Jun puts a small stone near the wall and rolls the ball toward it. The ball curves away and stops near Ronan's foot.

“Closer than that,” Jun says.

Ronan bends down and tries. His ball hits the stone and pushes it away.

“Does that count?”

“The stone is now closer to mine,” Jun says.

Leo laughs. He gets up from the step. He rolls the ball with his other hand. His ball stops a hand's width from the stone.

They choose three small stones. Each child has one. Now they must stop the ball beside their own stone. Ronan's first roll goes too far. His second stops short. On his third try, he uses a softer push.

The ball stops almost against his stone.

Leo makes a very serious face. He lies on his stomach to look at the gap. Jun lies down at the other side. Ronan stays standing.

“Is it close enough?”

“We need lunch before we can decide,” Jun says.

Ronan nudges his shoe. Jun rolls out of reach, laughing. A teacher passes them. She asks them to keep the path clear. They move back toward the wall.

When the bell rings, Leo picks up his bag with his good arm. Ronan offers to carry it to the classroom. Leo lets him, but keeps his water bottle.

“I can still carry one thing.”

At the desks, Ronan gives the bag back. Leo takes out a maths page. He has work to finish before his next activity. Ronan looks at the rows of numbers.

“More reading?”

“Numbers today.”

Ronan opens his own book. His single visit is over. Leo will go again on Saturday. He must finish his extra work first. Ronan still wants more visits. But Ronan has time to play this afternoon. He is pleased about that too.

At home, he shows Dad the soft roll. The ball stops beside the table leg. Dad moves his foot just in time. “Nearly got you!” Ronan says. He calls that a win.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

farther＝更远；shoulder＝肩膀；soft＝轻柔的。

## 理解问题

1. Leo为什么不愿投球？
2. Jun怎样改动游戏？

## 读句子

**Jun / lifts / the ball.** Jun／举起／球。
